subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?
related_links: Linear: ENG-4826 (Integrate scheduler flag into config system)
Jira: SUP-2215 (Dedicated tail latency / noisy-neighbor symptoms)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

Sofia — quick product question as we plan Q1 Dedicated reliability messaging.

We have a couple of Dedicated accounts (and one expansion) where the primary pain is p95 spikes when long-context summarization batches overlap with interactive chat traffic (support ticket SUP-2215 is a good example).

Is it realistic for us to offer the new mixed-workload scheduler as a *gated option* (feature flag / allowlist) for a specific Dedicated tier or specific routes, once it lands in runtime-1.19 default-off?

What I need to understand before I tell Sales/CS anything:
1) Risk profile: what’s the realistic failure mode if the classifier is wrong or traffic is bursty? (starvation, throughput collapse, oscillation?)
2) Operational requirements: what do SREs need in place (dashboards/alerts, rollback) to safely enable for a single customer?
3) Eligibility constraints: does this require a specific model/hardware SKU to be safe, or can we treat it as a generic runtime behavior?

If your answer is “not until we finish canary + ADR sign-off,” that’s fine — I just need a clear timeline/criteria so we can set expectations.

Thanks,
Lauren
Dedicated Product
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

Yes, in principle, but I’d strongly recommend we frame it as “opt-in experimental scheduling policy” until we complete canary + fairness validation.

Answers inline:

1) Risk / failure modes (what we’ve seen in testing so far)
- Misclassification: a “long” request ends up in short queue (worst-case short queue gets clogged, p95 regresses). We’re adding guardrails + sampling logs so we can diagnose.
- Priority inversion / batching interaction: the scary one is a long prefill batch blocking short work (we found one instance in a load test; fix is in flight as a regression test). This is why we’re making sure the scheduler is aware of prefill vs decode boundaries and not just prompt tokens.
- Starvation: if we over-prioritize interactive, long prompts can wait too long. Our policy includes a max-wait bound + periodic long-queue service, but we need more soak on bursty traces.

2) Operational requirements
- Must have per-class queue depth + wait time histograms on dashboards, and a clear rollback switch that returns to baseline FIFO.
- During first enablement, we should staff someone from runtime + SRE for the first hour.
- We need explicit rollback criteria (e.g., short-queue wait p95 > X for > Y minutes, error rate changes, backlog growth).

3) Eligibility
- It’s a runtime scheduler feature; doesn’t require a new API surface. But I’d prefer initial enables only on a small set of known-stable model+SKU combos (the same ones we’ll use in perf-canary).

Timeline: runtime-1.19 will contain the flag plumbing (default off). For customer-facing “gated option,” I want us to tie it to completion of ENG-4829 (canary plan + rollback criteria) + fairness sims. If we can keep canary clean, we could allowlist a single Dedicated customer in a controlled window.

Sean/Paula/Connor — anything you want to add on the rollout posture?

Sofia
EM, Scheduling


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 12:10 PM PST
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

+1 to Sofia’s framing.

From SRE perspective, I’m OK with *one* gated customer enablement as long as the following are true:

- Default remains OFF globally in 1.19.
- Enablement is reversible without redeploy (config/flag flip).
- We have starvation detection (long-queue max wait / queue depth slope) and short-queue tail breakdown on a single dashboard.
- The rollback triggers are written down *before* we enable, and we have a named on-call/owner for the window.

I’d rather not sell this as an SLA improvement yet. We should position it as “we’re testing a scheduling enhancement aimed at mixed workloads; we will run it under close monitoring.”

If helpful, we can make the enablement contingent on a short pre-canary in our perf-canary environment that’s similar to the customer distribution.

Sean
SRE Lead


---

From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 1:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

Adding a product/rollout lens:

I’m comfortable offering as a gated option for a specific tier *if we’re consistent about the contract language and approval path*.

Proposal:
- Name it as an “Experimental runtime scheduling policy (Mixed Workload Scheduler)” and require PM + SRE approval for enablement.
- Limit to: Dedicated + single region + pinned model version, at least for the first 1–2 customers.
- Require a runbook section: how to revert, what metrics to watch, and a decision tree if p95 improves but throughput drops.

Lauren — if you have the specific customer tier in mind, can you send me the tier definition and what you’d want the promise to be? I can help draft the internal enablement checklist and a customer-safe description.

Paula
PM, Rollouts


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 4, 2024 at 9:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

Release train constraints:

- We can ship the plumbing in runtime-1.19 as default-off and not mention it in external release notes.
- If we do a gated enablement, I want it to be config-only (no hotfix build) and I want a “kill switch” that’s safe even under load.

Sofia — please confirm the flag key + where it lives in the config system once PR lands. Also confirm whether enablement requires a runtime restart or can be picked up dynamically.

Lauren/Paula — if you need a go/no-go sign-off path, we can add a lightweight checklist in the release ticket so it doesn’t get lost.

Connor
Release Engineering


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Dec 5, 2024 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime-1.19) — can we offer as gated option for a Dedicated tier?

Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed.

I’ll position internally as: “experimental opt-in; not an SLA promise; limited scope; requires SRE + runtime approval + rollback plan.”

Customer/tier context (for Paula): this would be for our top Dedicated tier where we already do pinned model + reserved capacity, and the ask is specifically to stabilize interactive p95 during daily long-context jobs. I’m *not* asking to guarantee a number; just to offer an option to test with strict monitoring.

Action items I’ll take:
- I’ll draft a short enablement request template (customer, region, model/SKU, expected traffic mix, monitoring + rollback owner) and send for review.
- I’ll link SUP-2215 + the expansion notes so we have a concrete driver.

Sofia — once you have the canary criteria nailed down in ENG-4829, can you tag me? I want to tie any customer conversation to those criteria.

Sean — I’ll also sync with your team on what the minimal dashboard/alert set is for a first enablement.

Lauren
Dedicated Product
Redwood Inference
